memory_candidates.content: A noncomputable Decidable-valued declaration is a vacuity class, not merely a computability inconvenience: `noncomputable def f : Decidable p := ...` is unconditionally inhabited by `Classical.dec _`, so any hypothesis in its signature does no work and the same type is provable without it. This shape passes every pattern in the repository's prohibited-vacuous-definition list (`:= True`, `:= trivial`, `:= Unit`), compiles sorry-free, and therefore slips every mechanical gate. The escape is to make the Decidable fact an explicit argument about a concrete term (per-formula form) or to abstract the noncomputable function into an explicit function parameter plus its correctness iff (generic form) -- both then compile as plain computable defs. Diagnostic rule: a Decidable-valued declaration that REQUIRES the noncomputable keyword is carrying no content; treat that as a blocker on the statement shape, never as a keyword to add.
